issue.title: Housekeeping chop subprocesses die at startup with init_sys_streams Bad file descriptor until the lumberjack is restarted
issue.description:
Discovered while diagnosing the artifact_link_backfill 300s timeouts (sase-u9): a distinct, earlier failure mode on 2026-09-03 where housekeeping chop subprocesses crashed at interpreter startup, before any chop code ran.

Between 04:56 and 11:43 EDT on 2026-09-03, at least 7 hourly housekeeping ticks logged, for MULTIPLE chops (artifact_link_backfill AND bead_stale_cleanup):

```
Fatal Python error: init_sys_streams: can't initialize sys standard streams
Python runtime state: core initialized
OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor
  <no Python frame>
Error in <chop>: exit code 1
```

(see ~/.sase/axe/logs/lumberjack-housekeeping.log around lines 1180-1440, e.g. the 04:56:01 and 05:58:41 blocks).

The chop child process could not even initialize sys.stdin/stdout/stderr, meaning the file descriptors the long-lived lumberjack parent (interval 3600s) handed it were already closed/invalid at spawn time. The condition persisted across many hourly ticks and cleared only when the lumberjack was restarted at 16:39:36 ("Received shutdown signal" -> restart, PID 50412). That pattern points at the parent's stdout/stderr or output-capture pipe fds going stale in a long-lived orchestrator/lumberjack process (log rotation, laptop sleep/wake, or a leaked/closed capture pipe are the usual suspects on macOS), not at any individual chop.

Root cause is NOT yet established (hence size large): what is known is (a) it is chop-independent, (b) it is fatal to every chop run while present, (c) it self-clears on lumberjack restart, and (d) it produced 'exit code 1' error-digest noise that masked the separate sase-u9 timeout failure for most of a day.

task_type_fields.impact: While the condition is active, EVERY chop in the affected lumberjack fails at interpreter startup, so all housekeeping jobs (error digests aside) silently stop for hours; the resulting 'exit code 1' digests also obscure other real failures (it masked the sase-u9 timeouts for most of a day).
task_type_fields.location: axe lumberjack chop spawn path (long-lived housekeeping lumberjack parent handing stale stdio/capture fds to chop subprocesses); observed via ~/.sase/axe/logs/lumberjack-housekeeping.log
task_type_fields.repro: Not deterministically reproducible on demand: arises in a long-lived lumberjack after hours of uptime (likely across sleep/wake or log handling). Observed 2026-09-03 04:56-11:43 EDT on athena: every housekeeping chop tick failed with 'Fatal Python error: init_sys_streams: can't initialize sys standard streams / OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor / exit code 1' across multiple chops, until the 16:39 lumberjack restart cleared it. Check lumberjack-housekeeping.log lines ~1180-1440.
